boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented University of Minnesota–Twin Cities traditions, from the Rouser and Block M to annual campus gatherings.

cards.title: Rub Goldy’s Teeth
cards.subtitle: Goldy Gopher statue outside Coffman Memorial Union
cards.notes: Find the Goldy statue outside Coffman and rub its teeth as part of the campus good-luck ritual before a test or athletic event.
cards.short_summary: A newer campus ritual centered on the Goldy statue’s prominent teeth.
cards.evidence_claim: The University says many students rub the Goldy statue’s teeth for good luck before a big test or athletic event.
cards.access_notes: The source places the statue outside Coffman Memorial Union; confirm building access separately.

cards.title: Sing the Minnesota Rouser
cards.subtitle: University fight song
cards.notes: Listen for the Rouser at a Gopher sporting event and join the refrain when the band leads the crowd in the school song.
cards.short_summary: The University’s 1909 contest-winning fight song remains a core Gopher refrain.
cards.evidence_claim: The University’s marching-band history documents the Rouser’s 1909 contest origin and its regular use over generations.
cards.source_title: Minnesota Rouser | College of Liberal Arts
cards.access_notes: Typically encountered at athletic and marching-band events; event admission policies vary.

cards.title: Answer with Ski-U-Mah
cards.subtitle: Gopher rally cry
cards.notes: Notice the “Ski-U-Mah” call within the Rouser and at spirit occasions; use it as a campus rally cry, not as a claim about origin.
cards.short_summary: A distinctive Gopher exclamation embedded in the University’s fight-song tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: The University’s published Rouser lyrics include the repeated “Ski-U-Mah” rally cry.
cards.source_title: Minnesota Rouser | College of Liberal Arts
cards.access_notes: No separate access is required to learn the phrase; its public use occurs at spirit events.

cards.title: Spot the Block M
cards.subtitle: Minnesota Marching Band halftime formation
cards.notes: At a home football game or band program, watch for the Marching Band’s Block M formation and its visual link to University identity.
cards.short_summary: The Marching Band’s signature letter formation dates to its first halftime show.
cards.evidence_claim: The University says the Marching Band included the first Block M in its 1910 halftime show and that it is now a University symbol.
cards.source_title: History & Traditions | College of Liberal Arts
cards.access_notes: Shown during selected band performances and home football events; consult the relevant event listing.

cards.title: Mark Homecoming Week
cards.subtitle: Annual fall campus tradition
cards.notes: Use the annual Homecoming schedule to choose a campus event, then take in the broader week of Gopher spirit with alumni and students.
cards.short_summary: A campus-wide fall tradition with roots at Minnesota in 1914.
cards.evidence_claim: The University describes Homecoming as a Minnesota tradition since 1914 and lists its campus spirit events.
cards.access_notes: Homecoming 2026 is scheduled for October 19–24; individual events can have separate access rules.

cards.title: Line Up for the Homecoming Parade
cards.subtitle: Annual parade during Homecoming
cards.notes: Check the official route and time, then watch campus groups, alumni, and the Marching Band take part in the Homecoming Parade.
cards.short_summary: A long-standing Homecoming gathering that showcases University spirit in public.
cards.evidence_claim: The University calls the Homecoming Parade one of its longest-standing and most attended traditions; the 2026 parade is set for October 23.
cards.access_notes: Scheduled for Friday, October 23, 2026 at 6:30 p.m.; check the official page for route and updates.

cards.title: Follow Homecoming Royalty
cards.subtitle: Student ambassador court and royal selection
cards.notes: Read the current Homecoming Royalty materials to see how court members represent the University throughout Homecoming Week.
cards.short_summary: A long-running recognition tradition now framed around student representation.
cards.evidence_claim: The University states that Homecoming Royalty is a long-standing tradition and selects two court members as Homecoming Royals.
cards.access_notes: Applications and selection details are seasonal; use the official Homecoming page for current participation information.

cards.title: Begin at New Student Convocation
cards.subtitle: Official welcome for incoming students
cards.notes: If you are a new student, attend Convocation with your class and look for the academic-regalia ceremony that formally opens the year.
cards.short_summary: The University’s formal incoming-class welcome brings new students together before the academic year begins.
cards.evidence_claim: The University describes New Student Convocation as its official welcome to the incoming class and an annual tradition.
cards.source_title: A tradition of pride, purpose, and community at Convocation | Brief
cards.access_notes: Intended for incoming students during Welcome Week; attendance and logistics are communicated by the University.

cards.title: Close the Year at Spring Jam
cards.subtitle: Student-planned end-of-year campus festival
cards.notes: Check the official Spring Jam program for performances and activities, then choose an all-ages area rather than the separately restricted beer garden.
cards.short_summary: A student-planned campus festival that marks the end of the academic year.
cards.evidence_claim: The University describes Spring Jam as a student-planned campus festival celebrating the end of the school year.
cards.source_title: About Spring Jam | University of Minnesota
cards.access_notes: The 2026 event is listed for April 25 at Coffman Memorial Union; use all-ages festival areas and avoid the 21+ beer garden.

cards.title: Hear the Indoor Concert
cards.subtitle: Annual Northrop Marching Band concert
cards.notes: Reserve or obtain event information through Northrop, then experience the Marching Band’s annual indoor performance and Goldy appearance.
cards.short_summary: A long-running Northrop concert translating marching-band traditions to an indoor stage.
cards.evidence_claim: Northrop identifies the 2026 program as the 65th annual University of Minnesota Marching Band Indoor Concert.
cards.source_title: 65th Annual Marching Band Indoor Concert at Northrop
cards.access_notes: The official Northrop event page provides date, ticket, and accessibility details for the 2026 concert.
